summary: MarinerCommerce multi-region late-token tail surge and SLO exposure
description:
Issue summary: Between 2026-03-10T11:40Z and 2026-03-10T12:50Z MarinerCommerce experienced elevated tail latency on streaming and non-streaming generation across us-east and eu-west leading to SLO breaches for 95th/99th percentile token latency and several customer-visible timeouts. Impact: customer-facing checkout autocomplete and fraud-scoring features saw degraded response times and several 5xx responses when retries cascaded. Estimated affected requests: ~45k across both regions. Financial sensitivity: enterprise contract with SLO-based credits; potential exposure if we do not provide remediation and timeline.

High-level hypothesis: a combination of a kernel selection change on a quantized 70B variant and a routing decision that funneled high-concurrency short-sequence traffic to a newly provisioned pool with suboptimal batching parameters produced high tail latency. Smart-routing fallbacks increased request fanout and contributed to transient 5xxs as caches warmed.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Reproduce using a steady stream of short prompt requests (avg token output 8-12) to rw-llm-70B-quant in us-east with concurrency matching customer profile (~1200 rps).
2) Force routing to the 'new-pool' variant by applying the temporary policy used during the incident (see related_confluence_pages).
3) Observe token-level tail latency (p95/p99) and increased kernel splice failures in serving runtime logs.
4) Validate that changing batching window from 8ms to 2ms reduces tail.

investigation_notes: 11:41Z - Alerting triggered: increased p99 token latency (us-east) and elevated 5xx rate observed on customer route marinercommerce-checkout-autocomplete.
11:44Z - Support engaged SRE via #inc-marinercommerce and opened this ticket; first response to customer within 10 minutes per SLA.
11:50Z - SRE observed new kernel selection behavior in canary pool; correlate with runtime deploy earlier that morning (PR referenced).
12:05Z - Applied emergency routing override to avoid 'new-pool' for MarinerCommerce traffic; immediate partial improvement in 95th latency but p99 still high.
12:20Z - Tuned batching window on dedicated pools from 8ms -> 2ms and reduced batch_delay_ms_p95 to 6ms; observed stabilization of token tail latency.
12:35Z - Re-enabled controlled routing to new-pool with updated kernel whitelist and monitoring; no regression after 30m observation window.
Post-incident: customer reported intermittent UI timeouts during 11:50-12:15 window; credits discussion initiated.

Root cause: combination of kernel_selector regression (suboptimal kernel chosen for quantized path) + routing policy that concentrated short-sequence high-concurrency traffic onto under-tuned pool. Secondary factor: cold prefix caches increased KV cache misses causing additional token processing cost.

resolution_summary: Mitigation: (1) emergency routing override to bypass 'new-pool' for MarinerCommerce traffic; (2) reduce batching window on affected pools; (3) restrict kernel selector to avoid suboptimal kernel for short-sequence quantized paths. Root cause: regression in kernel selection algorithm combined with a routing policy that concentrated short-sequence high-concurrency requests onto an under-tuned pool, amplified by cold KV cache misses. Fixes: kernel selector PR merged and rolled to canary then prod (related_github_prs). Preventive controls: added a routing policy test for short-sequence traffic profiles and updated canary checklist to include tail-latency microbenchmarks for quantized variants. Customer impact: Short window of degraded UX (~30 minutes for visible timeouts) and possible SLA credit.
postincident_actions: 1) Runbook update: add explicit check for kernel selection behavior when onboarding quantized models (owner: R&D, due 2026-03-20).
2) Observability: create a dashboard for short-sequence token tail latency by model variant and region (owner: Observability, due 2026-03-18).
3) Routing policy: implement guardrail to avoid concentrating short-sequence high-concurrency traffic onto newly provisioned pools for first 2 hours (owner: Routing, due 2026-03-17).
4) Customer communication: prepare SLA credit calc and commercial note for MarinerCommerce (owner: Customer Success, due 2026-03-16).
5) Engineering QA: add microbenchmarks to CI for quantized kernels that simulate short outputs (owner: Infra QA, due 2026-03-24).
